title: Progressive JSON validation for streaming function calls and actionable error codes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Current function/tool-calling validation runs only after the model has finished producing the full call payload. For streaming outputs and long-running calls this causes bad developer UX and opaque error responses. We also lack a single canonical JSON schema format that supports incremental validation, field-level suggestions, and compatibility rules for legacy 'tool' shapes.

Goal: Implement a progressive/streaming JSON schema validation layer that: 1) validates partial JSON as it streams and emits deterministic early error classes; 2) adds a small set of machine-readable, stable error codes and human-friendly messages; 3) supports compatibility rules for legacy schemas (field aliases, deprecated names, graceful coercions) via a versioned compatibility manifest; and 4) exposes telemetry hooks for evaluating real-world error distributions and automatic remediation suggestions.

Scope: design and runtime parser + validator, SDK adapters (Python/JS) for surfaced error mapping, schema versioning format, migration guide, unit + integration tests, rollout plan with canary on dedicated and hosted endpoints. Not in scope: authoring UI for schema creation (will be follow-up).

Key constraints and trade-offs: incremental validation means we must accept partial parse states and avoid false positives on valid-but-incomplete payloads; we need to balance strictness with helpfulness (suggestions vs. failing fast). Telemetry should avoid PII and not increase latency beyond SLOs. Backwards compatibility: must support existing 'tool' manifests but allow opting into opt-in strict mode.

Proposed design highlights: 1) Schema manifest: a compact JSON schema extension with a 'streamHint' per field (e.g., requiredAfterTokens, preferExactMatch) and a compatibility section with aliases and coercion rules. 2) Validator modes: permissive (default) and strict (opt-in by caller); permissive emits warning-level errors and suggestion codes while still accepting recoverable coercions. 3) Streaming validator: incremental parse state machine that emits validation events with stable numeric error codes (e.g., 1001 MISSING_REQUIRED_PREFIX, 2002 TYPE_MISMATCH_AT_PATH) and suggestions payloads for fixes. 4) SDK mapping: SDK will map codes to idiomatic exceptions and include a short remediation snippet. 5) Runtime fallback: if strict validation fails mid-stream, runtime can signal model to continue in 'repair' mode or trigger fallback to a compatible model variant.

Deliverables: runtime validator impl, schema docs, SDK adapters, test corpus, rollout playbook, telemetry dashboards and alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Progressive validator integrated into runtime for text-to-function streaming path
Stable error code registry published and documented in docs.redwood.ai link
SDKs translate error codes into structured exceptions with remediation hints
Compatibility manifest versioning implemented and can alias deprecated field names
E2E tests covering partial stream cases, coercions, and strict-mode failures
Canary rollout on dedicated pool with latency impact < 5ms p50 and no P99 regression > 10%

comments: 2026-03-02 Maya Chen: Created ticket after working session with PM & SRE. Collected initial pain examples from CS (2 customers) where streaming outputs were rejected only at completion.

2026-03-04 Diego Ramirez: Prototype incremental validator produced first set of error codes; observed that partial-object detection needs heuristics to avoid spurious missing-field errors. Moving to implement 'requiredAfterTokens' hint.

2026-03-06 Anika Singh: SDK mapping design reviewed — proposal to include suggestion snippets as small code blocks. Concern: size of suggestion payloads over streaming; decided to cap snippet length and surface full docs link instead.
2026-03-08 QE: Collected 120 recorded function-call traces from sandbox; 17% would have triggered early suggestion in permissive mode. Added to test corpus.
2026-03-10 Security: Telemetry plan approved with PII redaction rules; telemetry will only include path-level error counts and anonymized token-length histograms.
2026-03-12 Diego Ramirez: Implemented error-code registry draft and pushed initial runtime branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4821. Need cross-team review from Docs and Observability.
